title: Give them a reason to refer you
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Why would someone tell a friend about you?
A student said: instead of asking do you have any friends who need my services, give people a reason to refer you on their own, based on an experience they had.

Jose described a story in the book of a dentist who turned a routine moment, a patient's braces coming off, into a celebration with a gong. He said the gong is a positive anchor: a sound they will never forget that anchors the celebration.
A student said: sometimes it is about converting the people in pre-engagement: someone refers you, then looks at your website and does not like it, so the referral never comes through.

groups.heading: Do not lead with a pitch

lines.text: Another said: it is a bad line to pitch someone right off the bat, and if you say you want to help them get more sales, their guard is up.
Jose said that a prospect who says they only get referrals is either operating so well that they do not need help, or is growing slowly and not saying so. You say: keep us in mind.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the moment in your service that could be a celebration.
Write the positive anchor you could give it.
Write what your website says to a referral.
Write how you will give people a reason to refer you.
Write your line instead of a pitch.

check.q: What did a student say to give people?
What did Jose call the gong?
What did a student say can stop a referral?
choices: A website they do not like

recap: Make an experience worth referring. Convert before you ask.
